speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your name, age, and when you first noticed these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions distributed only on the trunk, or do they also appear on the face, scalp, and extremities? Do the papules have a central umbilication or "dimple" when pressed?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of acute appendicitis is incorrect, as abdominal pain and fever are absent. Based on the pearly papules with central umbilication and daycare exposure, this is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
